craft_notes: Color: perception-overwhelmed (C1: sthayin transforms landscape into its body). Firing: dash-catalogue (dust, sun, moon — three strokes); unseen kept (not vanished). REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) passion-dust glossed -> killed: doctrine in C1, surface in L3/L4. (b) vanished for not-seen -> killed: seen-absence is the point. Read aloud: STRUCK by WA-ters, DUST-lies ON-earth — … SUN and MOON — THEY-are-NOT-seen. Abhinavagupta frame: grove as vibhāva, not backdrop — beauty as cause; kuṭaja-mockery and nīpa-release as anubhāva (consequents), not ornament; rasa overwhelming perception (dust obscuring sun/moon).

lines: Struck by waters, dust lies on earth —
sun and moon — they are not seen.
l4.sanskrit_cite: salilair vihataṃ rajaḥ kṣitau ravicandrāv api nopalakṣitau

c1_essence: Beauty is not decoration but cause: the groves shine for Kāma's sake, not the reverse. The grove is the vibhāva (determinant) of śṛṅgāra; the rasa overwhelms perception — dust of passion obscures sun and moon, new-cloud-drunk peacocks cry. The kuṭaja's mockery and the nīpa's release are consequents (anubhāva), not ornament: the poet sides with the humble tree over showy flowers. The bee kisses the yūthikā creeper. The rasa is aesthetic: the rasa IS the point.
